title: Component package metadata (`package.yaml`)
description: A backbone file schema (ADR-056) for the `package.yaml` of a component — a capability or an adapter. It type-checks every field the shipped package files use today and the blocks the connection-points, documentation-roots and friction records add. PERMISSIVE ON UNKNOWN KEYS: `additionalProperties` is left open at the top level and inside the new blocks, so an unknown key is not a schema error; `project_kit.package_validate` reports it as a WARNING with the nearest known key suggested (the renderer of ADR-056 point 4). Refusing unknown keys is the strict flip of Task #999, taken once every block is known. Known keys are strictly typed. Inventory of the keys in use when this schema landed, by `schema_version` — version 1 (adapter `claude-code`; capabilities `living-docs`, `software-analysis`, `software-engineering`): `schema_version`, `component {kind, name, version}`, `requires_backbone`, `footprint` (adapter), `description`, `requires_capabilities`; version 2 (capabilities `demo-recording`, `evidence`, `project-management`): `schema_version`, `component`, `description`, `requires_backbone`, `commands`, `aliases`, `runtime_ignore`. Version 2 marks a file that adopted the `commands:` block (COR-021 said the version bumps with it); no reader distinguishes the two, every field is optional in both, and this schema accepts both without bumping either. `provides` is admitted from COR-013 (hook implementations) though no shipped file uses it; no egress or privilege declaration exists in any package file — those live in the permission capability's own data.

schema_version.description: The package file's own schema version. Two values are in use, both accepted; a file without the key reads as 1.

description.description: One-line summary shown as the capability's command-group help (COR-021).

requires_backbone.description: Version range of compatible backbone versions, evaluated at install and upgrade (COR-010, COR-017). Parseability is checked in Python.

requires_capabilities.description: Declared dependencies on other capabilities, each a name and a version range (COR-030).

commands.description: The command tree the dispatcher registers under `pkit <capability>` (COR-021): a key is a token; a value carrying `script` is a leaf, any other value is a sub-group.

aliases.description: Alternative namespaces for the command group (`pm` for `project-management`).

validators.description: Validators this component registers with `pkit validate` (ADR-058): a mapping from a validator name (a word) to its entry, which names one leaf of this component's `commands:` tree by `command` — the leaf carries the `help` line and must declare `query-contract: true`. The umbrella addresses the validator `<component>:<name>` and runs the leaf's script from the project root with the one argument `--json`, the offline marker set and bounded like a predicate, reading one JSON document — and nothing else — from its standard output: `{"summary": ["..."], "findings": [{"severity": "error"|"warning"|"info"|"report", "location": "...", "message": "..."}]}` (a finding may add a `label`); diagnostics go to standard error. Only `error` fails the umbrella. An abnormal exit, a timeout, a leaf without the declaration or an answer that is not that document is an error finding, never a clean pass. `order` sorts the validator among the members (default 1000, after the backbone's, which take the orders below 1000). No shipped component uses it yet.

provides.description: Hook implementations this component answers, `{hook-name: implementation}` (COR-013). Reserved; no shipped file uses it.

footprint.description: Git-footprint paths this component deploys outside `.pkit/`, repository-relative (ADR-009).

runtime_ignore.description: Runtime-local file globs to git-ignore, repository-relative (ADR-009 rule 7).

name.description: Must equal the directory the component lives in (checked in Python).

version.description: The component's own version; it gates dependency edges. Parseability is checked in Python.

command-group.title: A level of the command tree

command-node.title: A command leaf or a sub-group
command-node.description: A leaf is detected by the presence of `script` at its level (COR-021).

script.description: Path of the script relative to the component root; must exist (checked in Python).

query-contract.description: The one constant declaration that this command honours the query contract (ADR-057 point 3; the literal is ADR-058's): bounded, deterministic, read-only, needing no network. Required on the command a validator names, and on every query command a capability registers. It grants nothing and is trusted, not enforced.

command.description: The leaf of this component's `commands:` tree that answers the validator's findings; must exist and declare `query-contract: true` (checked in Python). Its `help` is the validator's.

order.description: Where it sorts among the members: the backbone's members take the orders below 1000, and 1000 is the default.

connections.title: The `connections` block (COR-053 point 3)
connections.description: The roles this component provides and its connection points, split by whose point it is and which way it flows: `extension-points` are points this component defines (`accepts` data in, `offers` processes and events out); `extensions` are where it plugs into others (`contributes` data, `subscribes` to events, `depends-on` processes). Field layout beyond the two key pairs is this reference's choice (the lifecycle README).

roles.description: Qualified role names this component provides, `<publisher>::<role>` (COR-053 point 1). Every point it defines sits under one of these (checked in Python).

accepts.description: Data points this component defines, keyed by point address.

offers.description: Processes and events this component offers, keyed by point address.

data-point.title: An accepted data point (COR-053 point 2, COR-052)

schema.description: The point's companion JSON Schema, a path relative to the component's `schemas/` directory; must exist (checked in Python).

combination.description: How several fillers combine (COR-052 point 3): `single` — one filler answers, by precedence (project filler, then the one contribution — the contributor selection picks among several — then the default); `union` — entries merged by id, a project entry overriding one whole, two capabilities supplying one id an error; `additive` — entries merged, any collision an error, an entry leaving only through a removal override with its reason. `single` when absent.

inert.description: The inert policy (COR-052 point 6): what the point does when a filler meant to answer cannot — its version does not match, its command failed, its output is invalid. `fallback` resolves from the remaining fillers with a warning naming the one that failed; `fail` leaves the whole point unresolved, as a consumer feeding a gate or a check must declare. `fallback` when absent.

point-default.title: The definer's default for a data point (COR-052 point 2)

value.description: The default value, in the point's own shape: validated by the point's companion schema when the point resolves.

participation.description: How the default takes part: `always` — it contributes like any other filler, at the lowest precedence; `alone` — it answers only when no other filler is declared, and never because a declared filler broke.

offered-point.title: An offered process or event (COR-053 point 2)

process.description: For `kind: process` — the id of the process definition whose interface is offered (COR-036).

command.description: For `kind: event` — the writing command that emits it; must exist in `commands:` (checked in Python).

schema.description: For `kind: event` — the payload's companion JSON Schema under `schemas/`; must exist (checked in Python).

subject.description: For `kind: event` — the payload field naming the event's subject.

contribution.title: A contribution to another role's data point

schema_version.description: The point version this contribution targets (COR-053 point 5).

command.description: The command filler that supplies the data (COR-052 point 6); must exist in `commands:` and declare `query-contract: true` (checked in Python). It takes no parameter: run with `--json` alone, offline-marked and bounded, it prints the filler envelope `{schema_version, value}`.

value.description: The data this contribution supplies, written here rather than printed by a command: the point's value, validated by the point's companion schema when the point resolves. A contribution names `value` or `command`, not both (checked in Python).

subscription.title: A subscription to another role's event

command.description: The subscriber command the backbone runs after the producing command finishes; must exist in `commands:` (checked in Python).

depends-on.title: Generated process connections (COR-053 point 4)
depends-on.description: GENERATED, never hand-written: its single source is the process definitions' `depends_on`, regenerated by the refresh command and marked `generated: true`. The wiring resolver reads the entries; a stale copy fails validation once the refresh command ships (Task #995), since detecting it reads the process definitions. This schema fixes only the shape and the mark.

process.description: The upstream process, in the implementation form `<capability>:<process-id>` or the role form `<publisher>::<role>:<point>` (COR-038, COR-053 point 2).

mandatory.title: The mandatory mark (COR-053 point 6)
mandatory.description: Only with a reason; the mark without one is rejected.

locations.description: The sub-paths of this component's own documents, keyed by a location name, each relative to one of the project's documentation roots. Relative sub-paths only: no absolute path, no `..` (checked in Python).

root.description: Which documentation root the sub-path is under; `internal` when absent.

places.description: Where this component's anchored artefacts live: each place a path glob inside one of the component's declared documentation locations (`location`), or, without one, inside the project (checked in Python).

surface.description: Repository-relative path globs this component says ought to be described; paths in it that no artefact anchors to are reported as uncovered (COR-050 point 8).

location.description: A name from `docs.locations`; the place lies inside it.

point-description.description: Required prose: what the point means and what one may rely on. Nothing parses it (COR-053 point 3).

command-reference.description: A path through the `commands:` tree, tokens separated by spaces (`create issue`), landing on a leaf.

relative-path.description: Relative, no `..` segment — the Python check names the offending segment.
